speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development over the past five years, how many cases have been reported of working adults who have faced short-term family support challenges, such as taking care of young sick children or elderly sick parents who cannot be left in childcare centres or nursing homes respectively.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The main concern was the challenges they face in managing work and caregiving responsibilities, for example, when the children and elderly parents suddenly fall ill and care arrangements need to be made at the last minute.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: These leave provisions are on top of the parents' annual leave provisions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: In addition to leave provisions, to better help working adults manage their caregiving and working responsibilities, it is important for employers to also provide a family-friendly work environment, so that working caregivers also have the support and flexibility needed to balance work and caregiving responsibilities and duties.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: In anticipation of the rising eldercare needs as our population is ageing rapidly, we also have been studying how to better support caregivers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: As part of this process, we have sought the views of caregivers, aged care service providers, healthcare professionals, community organisations, as well as the tripartite partners.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We will share more details in response to the Motion on Support for Caregivers which would be tabled for discussion in this week's Sitting.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I understand that, yes, there are leave provisions for family care and childcare.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: But again, this varies, depending on employers, depending on the profession that you are in.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: So, there are parents, working adults who face difficulties when caring for many young children and caring for a few elderly parents, not just their own parents but including parents-in-law.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: So, are there current arrangements by any of the MSF partners in providing short-term family care and support at the moment?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: My second supplementary question is whether there are any plans by MSF, working with other partners, to pilot an integrated family care drop-in centre for such short-term care and support, whether it is at our existing childcare or senior care centres, or even in our polyclinics, for instance, for those who have children with contagious or infectious diseases like Hand, Foot, Mouth Disease (HFMD) or chickenpox, or elderly parents who have pneumonia, where some amount of medical care is required?

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: As for parents with young children where they need to put their children at the drop-in centres when their children fall sick and so on and so forth, this is something that is fairly complex.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: So, my Ministry has been looking at this.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: And I am glad that the Member has raised this.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: Once again, I thank the Member for the suggestions.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: I wonder in the case of daily-rated workers, who would constitute a significant proportion of the lower-income, whether the Ministry has plans to provide, for example, income support or other means of assistance for those who encounter these issues because they effectively cannot take leave.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: If they take leave, as they are daily-rated, they do not get paid at all.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: As this is something that is new, we will have to look at it.
